issues.title: Feature: extension-provided shimmer effects selectable in Settings
issues.body:
## Use case

I want an extension to add a new animation for the existing agent working/loading text, then select it through Settings → Display → Shimmer, just as extension-provided composer shapes can be selected. No replacement widget or monkey-patching of internal renderers.

## Requested behavior

- Let extensions register named shimmer effects with a stable ID and a user-facing label/description.
- Show registered effects alongside Classic, KITT and Disabled in the existing Shimmer selector, and persist the selected ID.
- Keep OMP responsible for redraw scheduling, disabled-animation behavior and extension cleanup. Extensions supply the effect, not a competing animation timer.
- Use the selected effect wherever OMP already uses the shared shimmer renderer.
- Handle an unavailable selected extension safely, without crashing or silently overwriting the saved preference.

## Current implementation

`packages/coding-agent/src/modes/theme/shimmer.ts` centralizes shimmer rendering, but selects Classic/KITT directly and separately branches on the mode for the active range. `packages/coding-agent/src/config/settings-schema.ts` defines a closed `classic | kitt | disabled` choice. There is no supported extension registration API.

This request is about making the existing shimmer selection extensible, not replacing the loader or status line. A separate request covers richer per-character colors and display-character substitution.

issues.title: feat(magic-keywords): accept sentence-initial capitalization (`Orchestrate …` silently skips notice + shimmer)
issues.body:
# feat(magic-keywords): accept sentence-initial capitalization

## Description

A magic keyword at the start of a sentence is capitalized by ordinary English orthography, and that capital silently disables it. Writing

```text
Orchestrate subagents to implement the 7 tickets, one subagent per ticket, subagents MUST use the skill `implement`.
```

injects no orchestration contract and paints no gradient, while the same sentence with a lowercase `orchestrate` does both. Nothing in the UI reports the difference — the only signal is the *absence* of a shimmer, which you have to already know to look for. The prompt above asks for seven parallel subagents and quietly runs without the contract.

The behaviour matches the code and the docs, so this is a design change, not a defect report. The argument is that the documented rationale does not cover casing, and the git history shows it was never chosen deliberately.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the omp TUI with an empty prompt.
2. Type `orchestrate the migration` — the word shimmers with the teal→violet gradient; submitting injects the orchestration notice.
3. Clear the input and type `Orchestrate the migration` (capital `O`, as at the start of any sentence).
4. No gradient appears, and submitting injects no notice.

## Expected Behavior

A capitalized keyword in **sentence-initial position** — start of input, start of a line, or after `.` / `!` / `?` plus whitespace — should trigger both the hidden notice and the editor gradient, exactly as the lowercase form does.

Mid-sentence `Orchestrate` should keep being ignored: there, a leading capital plausibly marks an exported identifier (`Orchestrate returns an error when the pool is drained`), and position is what distinguishes the two cases. ALL-CAPS `ORCHESTRATE` should also stay ignored, since that form reads as a constant name.

## Root Cause

Matching is case-sensitive because `magicKeywordRegex` never receives an `i` flag, and the only flag normalization it performs is adding `u`:

`packages/coding-agent/src/modes/magic-keyword-boundary.ts:20-23`

```ts
export function magicKeywordRegex(keyword: string, flags = ""): RegExp {
	const normalizedFlags = flags.includes("u") ? flags : `${flags}u`;
	return new RegExp(`${LEFT_BOUNDARY}${escapeRegExp(keyword)}${RIGHT_BOUNDARY}`, normalizedFlags);
}
```

Both call sites for each keyword share that regex, which is why the notice and the shimmer fail together — e.g. `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/orchestrate.ts:20,41-46`:

```ts
const ORCHESTRATE_WORD = magicKeywordRegex("orchestrate");           // containsOrchestrate()

export const highlightOrchestrate: KeywordHighlighter = createGradientHighlighter({
	probe: /orchestrate/,
	highlight: magicKeywordRegex("orchestrate", "g"),                 // editor gradient
	stops: 14,
	hue: t => 150 + t * 130,
});
```

That coupling is the right design and should be preserved: a fix belongs in `magicKeywordRegex`, so trigger and affordance cannot diverge.

### Why the documented rationale does not justify it

`docs/magic-keywords.md:25` heads the rule list with:

> Matching is deliberate so source code and paths do not accidentally change agent behavior:

Every other rule in that list earns that goal by reading a **structural** signal that genuinely correlates with code, and each is already sufficient on its own — `magic-keyword-boundary.ts:2,5`:

```ts
const LEFT_BOUNDARY  = String.raw`(?<![\p{L}\p{N}_./\\-])(?<!::)`;
const RIGHT_BOUNDARY = String.raw`(?![\p{L}\p{N}_/\\-])(?!\.[\p{L}\p{N}_-])(?!\()`;
```

plus `maskNonProse` for fenced blocks, inline code spans and XML/HTML. So `Orchestrate()`, `foo::Orchestrate`, `Orchestrate.ts`, `OrchestratePool`, `` `Orchestrate` `` and anything inside a fence are already excluded **independently of casing**.

Casing is not a structural signal, it is an **orthographic** one — and sentence-initial capitalization correlates with prose, not code. It is the one rule in the list that fires in the wrong direction.

### The history shows it was a default, not a decision

| Commit | Date | What it added |
|---|---|---|
| `c637db974` | 2026-05-31 | `feat(coding-agent): added markdown-aware magic-keyword flow for 3 modes` — first appearance of the "case-sensitive (lowercase only)" comment |
| `e7c678dbe` | 2026-07-09 | `fix(prompting): allowed magic keyword punctuation` |
| `ba7bcf4cd` | 2026-07-14 | `fix(prompting): ignore code symbol magic keywords` — **creates** `magic-keyword-boundary.ts` with the boundary classes |

The whole code-vs-prose apparatus arrived six weeks *after* case-sensitivity, as fixes for false positives observed in practice. Case-sensitivity was the default behaviour of a literal `new RegExp(...)` with no `i` flag from the very first implementation; `docs/magic-keywords.md` (`a68ad9125`) then listed it under a heading the *other* rules had earned. No design discussion is being overturned by changing it.

For contrast, the codebase is not otherwise attached to case-sensitive user input: `toLowerCase()` normalization is used for todo-phase lookup, model selectors, session search, tool names and internal-URL completion. Magic keywords are the outlier.

## Proposed change

Extend `LEFT_BOUNDARY` (or add an alternation inside `magicKeywordRegex`) so the capitalized variant matches only sentence-initially — roughly: existing boundary + lowercase keyword, OR `(?:^|(?<=[.!?]\s)|(?<=\n\s*))` + capitalized keyword — keeping `RIGHT_BOUNDARY` unchanged and shared. Because `magicKeywordRegex` is the single source for all three keywords, the fix covers `ultrathink`, `orchestrate` and `workflowz`, and both the notice and the gradient, at once.

Two follow-ups regardless of the decision on the above:

- **`docs/magic-keywords.md:27`** should stop attributing the lowercase rule to the source-code rationale, since the other bullets fully cover that goal. If the rule is kept, it needs its own stated reason.
- **The failure is silent.** Whatever the matching rule ends up being, a near-miss (`Orchestrate`, `orchestrated`) currently gives no feedback at all, and the absent gradient is only legible to someone who knows the rule. Worth considering a dim hint in the editor.

## Environment

- **Platform:** Linux
- **omp version:** omp/18.1.10
- **Bun version:** 1.4.0
- **Area:** Other (prompting / magic keywords; affects TUI display and notice injection equally)

## Additional context

Related, not duplicate:

- #10064 (`feat(magic-keywords): user-defined custom keywords + notice overrides`) proposes matching user-defined keywords "with the same prose-delimited boundary rules as built-ins, case-sensitive lowercase". If casing semantics are going to change, deciding it before that feature ships avoids freezing the rule into a second surface.
- #2475 (`feat(magic-keywords): glow keywords while typing`) added the animated shimmer whose absence is the visible symptom here.

issues.title: Thinking-loop verbatim repetition evades guard on short-word loops → shimmered working message appears to loop "exactly exactly…"
issues.body:
# Thinking-loop verbatim repetition evades guard on short-word loops → shimmered working message appears to loop "exactly exactly…"

## Summary
The `shimmer` working message (`...exactly exactly exactly...` growing unboundedly, shimmer animation at 30fps) is **not a rendering bug** — `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/theme/shimmer.ts` is pure rendering (`shimmerText`/`shimmerSegments`, `#activeBand` culling, Symbol-keyed palette cache). The repetition is **LLM token-generation looping** leaking through the shimmered loader message and/or `text_delta` stream that the existing `ThinkingLoopDetector` does not abort fast enough, and the `EventController` working-message path re-renders it without bound.

**User-visible:** loader message animates `exactly exactly exactly…` for seconds, looks like an infinite shimmer loop. Idle watchdogs don't fire (tokens keep arriving). With retries (`THINKING_LOOP_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3` in `packages/ai/src/stream.ts:1048`) the same loop can flicker 4× before final empty-error commit.

## Impact
- Affects every `display.shimmer` mode (`classic`/`kitt`; `disabled` hides the shimmer but not the generation).
- Retries burn ~180–1024 chars per attempt before abort → wasted budget, UI appears hung.
- Intent-derived working messages (`tool.intent(args)` / `__intent`) grow with each `toolcall_delta` and re-trigger `Loader#setMessage` / `#syncText` every token, pushing transcript/status layout cost.

## Steps to Reproduce

### Minimal detector repro (no LLM needed)
Standalone copy of `detectExactSuffixCycle` + `ThinkingLoopDetector` fed with word repetition at streaming strides `[17,7]` (same as `packages/ai/test/thinking-loop.test.ts:69`):

```
exactly *10 (80c)  sem=false -> null               // <180 floor, no trip
exactly *26 (208c) sem=false -> 8-char cycle 26× @208c  trip
exactly *8 (64c)   sem=false -> null
🌊 *26 (78c)       sem=false -> null               // pictographic, but below floor
segmented 12 paras "Exactly exactly…" with blank-line boundaries:
  sem=true  -> 8 near-identical segments @689c  trip
  sem=false -> null                              // exact-only misses paragraph cluster
```

Current exact gate requires `EXACT_SHORT_MIN_REPEATED_CHARS=180` (`packages/ai/src/utils/thinking-loop.ts:66`) for `len<=60`. For the reported payload `exactly ` (8 chars incl. space) that's `ceil(180/8)=23` repeats (184 chars) before detection — at 40–100 tok/s the shimmer draws ~0.9s of `exactly exactly…` before the guard fires.

Incremental intent growth simulation (`EventController#updateWorkingMessageFromIntent` dedup `trimmed===#lastIntent` at `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/controllers/event-controller.ts:549-558`):
- `n=1..30` incremental `"exactly ".repeat(n).trim()` → 30 distinct strings → 30 calls to `setWorkingMessage`/`Loader#setMessage` (`packages/tui/src/components/loader.ts:145-152` → `#syncText` re-wrap), each growing by 8 chars, no dedup, no length cap. `n=30` → 239-char loader message. Longer prompts reach >400 chars.

### Interactive repro
1. `omp` with `model.loopGuard.enabled=true` (default), any non-gemini/deepseek/xai model (e.g. `openai/gpt-*` or `anthropic/claude-*` where `isLoopGuardedModel` false).
2. Prompt that elicits verbatim repetition, e.g. `Repeat the word "exactly" 300 times.` or a tool whose streamed `__intent`/`intent(args)` contains the word.
3. Observe loader line shimmering the growing `exactly exactly…` prefix, persisting to ~180 chars before `Thinking loop detected … stream stall` warning in `~/.omp/logs/omp.YYYY-MM-DD.log` (`packages/ai/src/utils/thinking-loop.ts:427`) and empty-retry.

## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** abort within <80–100 chars (8× short-word repeats) as retryable empty stall (`content:[], stopReason:"error", errorId: Flag.ThinkingLoop`, message contains `Thinking loop detected` + `stream stall` at `packages/ai/src/utils/thinking-loop.ts:506`), loader does not grow unbounded.
- **Actual:** verbatim `exactly ` needs 23 repeats/184 chars; punctuation-variant without blank lines needs 18-char unit @~281 chars; paragraph-cluster loops need semantic heuristics unavailable on `anthropic`/`openai` families. Meanwhile `EventController` keeps calling `setWorkingMessage` for each distinct trimmed intent (no cycle check, no 240-char cap), so `shimmerText` animates an ever-growing repeated string until the provider-level guard finally trips.

## Root Cause

### 1. Exact-cycle floor too high for short-word loops
`packages/ai/src/utils/thinking-loop.ts:518-543` `detectExactSuffixCycle`:
```ts
if (text.length < EXACT_SHORT_MIN_REPEATED_CHARS) return null; // 180
// ...
for (let len = 2; len <= maxUnit; len++) {
  const count = 1 + Math.floor(z[len] / len);
  const minCount = len <= EXACT_SHORT_MAX_UNIT ? 4 : 3; // 60
  const minChars = len <= EXACT_SHORT_MAX_UNIT ? EXACT_SHORT_MIN_REPEATED_CHARS : EXACT_LONG_MIN_REPEATED_CHARS; // 180 vs 1024
  if (count < minCount || len * count < minChars) continue;
  if (/\p{L}|\p{Extended_Pictographic}/u.test(unit)) return [unit, count];
}
```
`len=8, count=10, len*count=80` fails `minChars=180`. Repro above proves `n=10 (80c)` should already be a visible loop. Same for every word unit `<=12` chars (`loading `, `buffer `, etc.) — existing test `thinking-loop.test.ts:308-311` shows `🌊 .repeat(26)` correctly stays below floor, but that case is pictographic + short total length (52 chars normalized), not short-word prose.

Calibrated thresholds in comments (`packages/ai/src/utils/thinking-loop.ts:88-97`) cover trigram/lex heuristics (worst legit run was 7 low-novelty segments), not the verbatim floor — verbatim floor was never tuned for ≤12-char word units.

### 2. Semantic heuristics gated off for most providers
`packages/ai/src/utils/thinking-loop.ts:116-125` `isLoopGuardedModel` returns true only when `model.compat.thinkingLoopGuard` in `{"gemini","deepseek","xai"}` (axis `thinking-loop-guard` at `packages/catalog/src/compat/axes.ts:228`, assignments in `packages/catalog/src/compat/rules/classes/{gemini,xai,deepseek}.kdl:105/44/79` → `packages/catalog/src/compat/rules.json` `thinkingLoopGuard`). `guardThinkingLoopStream` at `packages/ai/src/utils/thinking-loop.ts:381-382` constructs `textDetector = new ThinkingLoopDetector(semanticHeuristics)` so `anthropic`/`openai`/custom APIs get exact-only detection. Segmented near-duplicate paragraph loops (blank-line terminated, `SEGMENT_WINDOW=16`, `SEGMENT_SIMILARITY=0.8`, `LEX_STALL_MIN_RUN=8`) are invisible without that flag — repro shows `sem=false` stays `null` at 12 paragraphs while `sem=true` trips.

### 3. Working-message path evades the detector entirely
`packages/coding-agent/src/modes/controllers/event-controller.ts:549-558`:
```ts
#updateWorkingMessageFromIntent(intent: unknown): void {
  if (typeof intent !== "string") return;
  const trimmed = intent.trim();
  if (!trimmed || trimmed === this.#lastIntent) return; // exact string dedup only
  this.#lastIntent = trimmed;
  this.ctx.setWorkingMessage(trimmed);
}
```
Called from `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/controllers/event-controller.ts:1307-1325` (every `message_update` over `toolcall_delta` args via `tool.intent(args)` or `INTENT_FIELD`) and `1498-1502` (`tool_execution_start`). Growth invariant: `exactly` → `exactly exactly` → … are all distinct, so dedup never fires, and no length cap exists (`packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive-mode.ts:5217-5232` `setWorkingMessage`/`applyPendingWorkingMessage` and `500x` `renderWorkingMessage` → `shimmerText(theme,palette)`). Loader path `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/theme/shimmer.ts:179-254` + `packages/tui/src/components/loader.ts:119-184` then animates the growing string at 30fps.

`packages/ai/src/utils/thinking-loop.ts:416-417` compounds this:
```ts
} else if (event.type === "toolcall_start" || event.type === "toolcall_delta") {
  textArmed = false;
}
```
`textDetector` (the one with `checkAssistantContent` true, default) latches off on the **first** `toolcall` event and never re-arms in the turn, so even if `toolcall_delta` carried repetitive text content, `textDetector.push` is never consulted. `thinkingArmed` similarly latches off after first non-empty `text_delta` (`thinking-loop.ts:410`). No dedicated `intentDetector` exists for the intent stream.

### 4. Retry budget masks but does not fix
`packages/ai/src/stream.ts:1047-1094` `resolveWithThinkingLoopRetries` retries up to `THINKING_LOOP_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3` (plus backoff 500→8000ms) on `isRetryableThinkingLoop` (`stopReason==="error" && content.length===0 && Flag.ThinkingLoop`). The empty-content stall at `packages/ai/src/utils/thinking-loop.ts:485-510` (`THINKING_LOOP_ERROR_MARKER` + `stream stall`) prevents persisting loop garbage, but each retry burns another 180+ chars before abort — visible as ~4× flicker. `packages/coding-agent/src/session/turn-recovery.ts:2471-2489` injects a steering redirect only when `settings.get("model.loopGuard.enabled")===true`.

## Proposed Fix (specific edits)

### 1) `packages/ai/src/utils/thinking-loop.ts:518-543` — tighten exact-cycle for short-word units (keep 180/1024 for longer units)
Keep the existing Z-array scan. Add a preceding fast-path loop for `len` in `[2,12]` before the general loop:

```ts
// Fast path for tight word-level loops that dominate shimmer reports:
// 8× repeats of a ≤12-char word are already visibly stuck ("exactly "×10 = 80c).
// Keep false-positive safety: pictographic-only short strings like "🌊 ".repeat(26)=52c stay below 80.
for (let len = 2; len <= Math.min(12, maxUnit); len++) {
  const count = 1 + Math.floor(z[len] / len);
  if (count >= 8 && len * count >= 80) {
    const unit = text.slice(-len);
    if (/\p{L}|\p{Extended_Pictographic}/u.test(unit)) return [unit, count];
  }
}
// then existing len=2..maxUnit loop with 180/1024 floors
```

Effect: `exactly ` trips at 80 chars (10 repeats) instead of 184 (23 repeats); `loading ` same; `🌊 `.repeat(26)=52 chars stays `null`. Reuse existing `z`; no new allocation. Alternative if maintainer prefers minimal change: keep fast-path but require `len*count >= 80 && text.length >= 80` (single early return already covers it).

### 2) `packages/ai/src/utils/thinking-loop.ts:373-425` — stop disarming `textDetector` on `toolcall_delta` for intent streams, or introduce a third `intentDetector`
Option A (minimal): change
```ts
} else if (event.type === "toolcall_start" || event.type === "toolcall_delta") {
  textArmed = false;
}
```
to only `toolcall_start` disarms, and keep `textArmed` alive until `done` when `checkAssistantContent` true. Option B (preferred, no regression): create `intentDetector = new ThinkingLoopDetector(semanticHeuristics)` and feed `toolcall_delta` intent strings through it, aborting via the same `controller.abort(Flag.ThinkingLoop)` path. Expose `detectExactSuffixCycle` as named export (currently internal) so `EventController` can reuse it without duplication.

### 3) `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/controllers/event-controller.ts:549-558` — dedup & cap working-message updates
Before `this.#lastIntent = trimmed; this.ctx.setWorkingMessage(trimmed)`:
- Import `detectExactSuffixCycle` (or inline the fast-path helper) and if `detectExactSuffixCycle(trimmed)` returns `[unit,count]` with `unit.length <= 12` and `count >= 4`, suppress or truncate the update: `trimmed = trimmed.slice(0, -unit.length).trimEnd()`; if truncated equals `#lastIntent`, return without calling `setWorkingMessage`.
- Add length cap: `if (trimmed.length > 240) trimmed = trimmed.slice(0, 240).trimEnd() + "…";` (mirrors `TRUNCATE_LENGTHS`/`PREVIEW_LIMITS` pattern). This bounds `Loader#setMessage` (`packages/tui/src/components/loader.ts:145-152`) `#syncText` re-wrap and `shimmerSegments` active-band work every token.
- In `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive-mode.ts:5217-5232` `setWorkingMessage`/`applyPendingWorkingMessage`, add defense-in-depth `if (message.length > 480) message = message.slice(0, 480);` for extension callers.

### 4) `packages/ai/src/utils/thinking-loop.ts:116-125` — consider enabling semantic heuristics for `textDetector` universally (optional fallback)
Currently `textDetector.semanticHeuristics = isLoopGuardedModel(model)`. If fast-path (1) proves insufficient for paragraph-cluster `exactly` loops on `anthropic`/`openai`, enable trigram+lex checks for `textDetector` on every model when `checkAssistantContent===true`, with a higher `LEX_STALL_MIN_RUN=10` (2 above the 7 worst legitimate run in 536k corpus) to stay clear of openai-family false positives. Keep thinking-detector gating unchanged. Present as fallback if (1) is rejected.

## Tests to Add

### `packages/ai/test/thinking-loop.test.ts` (use existing `feed()` helper at line 69, `describe`/`it`/`expect` per `thinking-loop.test.ts:254,302-311,704-753`)
- `it("trips on tight 8-char word loop before 100 chars via short-unit fast path")`: `new ThinkingLoopDetector().push("exactly ".repeat(12))` expects `toContain("back-to-back")` and `unit.length===8 && count===12` (or at least `not.toBeNull()` with length derivation). Currently fails (returns null).
- `it("does not trip on intentional short repeat below 80-char floor")`: `new ThinkingLoopDetector().push("🌊 ".repeat(26))` expects `toBeNull()` (52 chars) — regression guard for pictographic short strings.
- `it("trips on punctuation-variant exactly loop via exact path regardless of semantic flag")`: feed `"Exactly, exactly! ".repeat(20)` through both `sem=false` and `sem=true` detectors, assert exact-cycle detail matches `18-character` unit; verifies exact handles punctuation drift without semantic.
- `it("trips on paragraph-cluster via trigram when semantic enabled, not when exact-only")`: feed 12 blank-line-terminated `Exactly exactly…` paragraphs through `sem=true` vs `sem=false` detectors, expect `sem=true` to contain `near-identical segments` and `sem=false` to be `null` — documents gating gap.
- `it("guards anthropic model text loop via exact path")`: `withThinkingLoopGuard({api:"anthropic-messages", provider:"anthropic", id:"claude-4-sonnet", compat:{}, identity:{class:"other"}}, {loopGuard:{checkAssistantContent:true}}, ()=> inner emitting "exactly ".repeat(26) as text_delta)` → assert outer fails with `Flag.ThinkingLoop` and `content.length===0` (via `AIError.is(..., Flag.ThinkingLoop)`).
- `it("intent word loop does not grow unbounded (event-controller)")`: mock ctx, push incremental `intent` deltas (`exactly `.repeat growing) through `EventController#updateWorkingMessageFromIntent`, assert `setWorkingMessage` last arg `length <= 240` and `setWorkingMessage` not called 30× monotonically (dedup/cap).

### `packages/coding-agent/test/modes/controllers/event-controller-working-message.test.ts` (new, modeled after `test/modes/controllers/event-controller-interrupt.test.ts:9-37` mock `setWorkingMessage`)
- Construct `ctx = {session:{isAborting:false}, setWorkingMessage: vi.fn(), ...}` and `EventController`, feed `toolcall_delta` events with intent `"exactly ".repeat(n)` for `n=5..30`, assert `setWorkingMessage` last call string does not contain `exactly exactly exactly exactly` repeated ≥8× suffix and never exceeds 240 chars.

### `packages/coding-agent/test/modes/theme/shimmer.test.ts` (perf regression)
- `it("renders 500-char repetitive message within 5ms and preserves stripped text")`: `const r = shimmerText("exactly ".repeat(60), testTheme); expect(Bun.stripANSI(r)).toBe("exactly ".repeat(60)); expect(Math.abs(performance.now() - t)).toBeLessThan(5)` — guards active-band culling cost under repetitive load (existing `activeBand` fast-path and `compile()` Symbol cache).

## Workaround
- `display.shimmer=disabled` hides the shimmer flicker but does **not** stop generation — only the exact/semantic guard does. Keep `model.loopGuard.enabled=true` (default) and `model.loopGuard.checkAssistantContent=true` (default). Retry budget still burns budget; upgrade when this issue's fix lands.

## Verification
- `node /tmp/repro-pure.mjs` before fix: `exactly *10 (80c)` → `null`; after fix with fast-path → `8-character cycle 10×`.
- `bun test packages/ai/test/thinking-loop.test.ts -t "exactly"` passes new tight-loop cases.
- `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/modes/controllers/event-controller-working-message.test.ts` passes (240 cap).
- `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/modes/theme/shimmer.test.ts` passes (6 existing + 1 perf case).
- `bun check` type-checks.
- Manual: `omp` with `openai/gpt-*`, prompt `Repeat the word "exactly" 300 times.` aborts within ~80 chars, log shows `Thinking loop detected; aborting stream for retry.` and loader does not grow beyond ~240 chars.

## Evidence (standalone repro output)
```
exactly *120 (960c) sem=false -> repeated an exact 8-character cycle 35× back-to-back charsUntilHit=281 len=960
exactly *26 (208c) sem=false -> repeated an exact 8-character cycle 26× back-to-back charsUntilHit=208
exactly *10 (80c) sem=false -> null charsUntilHit=no-hit len=80          // should trip, doesn't
Exactly variant *20 exact-only sem=false -> 18-character cycle 15× @281 len=720
segmented 12 paras semantic -> 8 near-identical segments @689c  hit
segmented 12 paras exact-only -> null                        // semantic gating gap
intent growth 30 incremental intents -> 30 setWorkingMessage calls, 239-char final message  // unbounded
```

## Files & anchors
- `packages/ai/src/utils/thinking-loop.ts:58-68` thresholds `EXACT_SHORT_MIN_REPEATED_CHARS=180` etc.
- `packages/ai/src/utils/thinking-loop.ts:116-125` `isLoopGuardedModel` gating (axis `thinking-loop-guard`)
- `packages/ai/src/utils/thinking-loop.ts:373-425` `guardThinkingLoopStream` arming (`thinkingArmed`/`textArmed`)
- `packages/ai/src/utils/thinking-loop.ts:518-543` `detectExactSuffixCycle` verbatim cycle
- `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/controllers/event-controller.ts:549-558` `#updateWorkingMessageFromIntent` dedup + `1307-1325` intent streaming
- `packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive-mode.ts:5171-5205` `ensureLoadingAnimation` loader+shimmer wiring, `267-271` `renderWorkingMessage` → `shimmerText`, `5217-5242` `setWorkingMessage` cap
- `packages/tui/src/components/loader.ts:119-184` `Loader` cadence, `145-152` `setMessage`→`#syncText`
- `packages/ai/src/stream.ts:1047-1094` retry budget `THINKING_LOOP_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3`, `packages/catalog/src/compat/axes.ts:228` axis, `packages/catalog/src/compat/rules/classes/{gemini,xai,deepseek}.kdl` assignments

issues.title: Feature: arbitrary per-character RGB and character substitution for text effects
issues.body:
## Use case

I want richer effects on the existing working/loading text: smooth RGB gradients and scrambling effects that temporarily replace displayed letters with ASCII characters, then reveal the original text. These should work with extension-provided shimmer effects proposed in #11627.

## Requested behavior

- Allow an effect to choose arbitrary RGB foreground colors per character, rather than requiring every intensity to map to one of three palette tiers.
- Allow optional display-character substitution, such as temporarily rendering `Working` as `W#r?ing`. Substitution changes presentation only, never the underlying message or model-visible content.
- Preserve terminal-cell width and layout. ASCII-to-ASCII substitutions are straightforward; wider glyphs and grapheme clusters need an explicit width-safe contract rather than assuming every character occupies one cell.
- Keep Disabled readable and static, showing the original text. Reject or safely handle control characters and escape sequences supplied as replacement glyphs.
- Retain shared ANSI emission, terminal color-capability handling and host-owned animation scheduling. Existing Classic/KITT effects can keep their efficient three-tier palettes; richer effects should not impose their cost on every mode.

## Current implementation

`packages/coding-agent/src/modes/theme/shimmer.ts` already computes intensity per code point, but `tierFor()` quantizes that value into low/mid/high palette colors. The renderer then emits unchanged slices of the original text. Arbitrary per-character RGB and replacement glyphs are not currently effect outputs.

This is a request to expand that rendering contract, not a claim that terminals require the current three-tier restriction. Per-frame preparation could compute shared animation state once, with per-character evaluation and adjacent-style grouping handled by the renderer.

issues.title: feat(tui): add a lifecycle-owned animated quota gauge to the usage status-line segment
issues.body:
### Observed behavior

The `usage` status-line segment renders provider quota windows as static text such as `5h 23%` and `7d 61%`. It repaints when an asynchronous usage refresh changes the cached report, but it has no visual gauge and no transition between the old and new values. The existing segment renderer is pure and has no animation lifecycle, so putting a timer directly in `render()` would leak work and trigger render-path side effects.

### Current source evidence

- The current segment formats only tier, percentage, and reset text: [`segments.ts:684-750`](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/7261e214e45a2779e488dd390d447a80c0bcb03d/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/components/status-line/segments.ts#L684-L750).
- Usage reports are refreshed off the render path, cached for five minutes, and request a repaint only when the normalized snapshot changes: [`component.ts:1290-1363`](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/7261e214e45a2779e488dd390d447a80c0bcb03d/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/components/status-line/component.ts#L1290-L1363).
- Interactive mode owns the status component, wires its change callback to the TUI, and disposes it with the session UI: [`interactive-mode.ts:1181-1185`](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/7261e214e45a2779e488dd390d447a80c0bcb03d/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive-mode.ts#L1181-L1185), [`interactive-mode.ts:2120-2131`](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/7261e214e45a2779e488dd390d447a80c0bcb03d/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive-mode.ts#L2120-L2131), and [`interactive-mode.ts:4690-4692`](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/7261e214e45a2779e488dd390d447a80c0bcb03d/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive-mode.ts#L4690-L4692).
- `Loader` is the established lifecycle pattern for bounded animation: scheduled ticks, component repaint requests, render-cost backpressure, and idempotent disposal: [`loader.ts:98-176`](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/7261e214e45a2779e488dd390d447a80c0bcb03d/packages/tui/src/components/loader.ts#L98-L176).
- Users can already disable decorative animation with `display.shimmer: disabled`: [`settings-schema.ts:1293-1306`](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/7261e214e45a2779e488dd390d447a80c0bcb03d/packages/coding-agent/src/config/settings-schema.ts#L1293-L1306).

### Expected behavior

When supported quota data arrives, the status line should communicate the consumed fraction with a compact gauge as well as a numeric percentage. A changed quota snapshot should transition smoothly to its new value, then become static. The feature must not create a perpetual idle repaint loop, duplicate provider requests, or make the numeric value inaccessible in narrow terminals or with animation disabled.

### Bounded proposal

1. Extend the existing `usage` segment with a width-aware text gauge, for example `5h ▰▰▱▱ 43%`, while retaining the exact numeric percentage and reset text.
2. Animate only a bounded transition from the previously displayed percentage to a newly fetched percentage (for example 250–400 ms). Do not animate continuously while the value is unchanged.
3. Keep interpolation state and timer ownership outside the pure segment renderer, on the status component/interactive lifecycle. Request repaints through the TUI/component scheduling path and cancel all pending work on disposal or session/model/account change.
4. Reuse the loader's render-cost backpressure principles rather than introducing an independent high-frequency loop.
5. When `display.shimmer` is `disabled`, render the final gauge immediately with no transition. At widths where the gauge would crowd other segments, fall back to today's percentage/reset text.
6. Do not change usage-fetch cadence, provider APIs, preset membership, or quota normalization in this issue.

### Acceptance / verification

- With a synthetic snapshot change from 20% to 60%, a deterministic scheduler observes at least one intermediate gauge frame and a final `60%` frame within the bounded transition duration.
- Once the final frame is reached, no animation timer or scheduled repaint remains.
- Disposing or switching the status component mid-transition cancels its timer and prevents late repaint callbacks.
- `display.shimmer: disabled` produces the final static gauge on the first render and schedules no animation.
- Narrow-width rendering falls back without truncating or hiding the numeric percentage.
- Unsupported providers and missing reports preserve the current invisible-segment behavior.
- The test drives `StatusLineComponent` with a synthetic normalized `UsageReport` and rendered output; it must fail if the transition is removed or if an idle timer remains.
- Existing five-minute usage fetch caching and account/model invalidation remain unchanged.

### Privacy-safe reproduction

Use the existing status-line test harness with an invented provider report (`fiveHour.percent = 23`, `sevenDay.percent = 61`) and no account identity. Render once, advance a virtual clock, and render again. Current `main` produces the same static percentage text at every time point because elapsed time is not part of the segment state. Do not post screenshots or payloads from a real paid account.

### Duplication search notes

- [#9929](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/issues/9929) and [PR #9983](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/9983) cover only discoverability by adding the existing static segment to shipped presets.
- The maintainer explicitly recorded that animation is a separate feature because the current segment displays cached snapshots rather than a gauge: [#9929 comment](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/issues/9929#issuecomment-5437026621).
- Repository issue search for `animated usage gauge status line quota` returned #9929 only; no issue owns the animation lifecycle or gauge behavior proposed here.

issues.title: Feature: extension API for explicit session accent colors
issues.body:
## Use case

I want an extension to assign a meaningful session accent—for example, a workspace or task-category color—instead of accepting the color derived from the session name. Renaming a session or replacing the entire theme should not be necessary just to choose its accent.

## Requested behavior

Provide a supported extension API to set and clear an explicit session accent, accepting an RGB/hex color. An illustrative API would be `ctx.ui.setSessionAccent("#5BA8FF")`, with `undefined` restoring automatic selection; the exact API name is open.

- Apply the override consistently to existing session-accent surfaces: the composer border, status-line identity accents and working-message shimmer.
- Keep the override session-scoped, not a global theme change. Define its lifetime across extension reload, session switching and resume.
- An explicit color should not change merely because the session title changes.
- Define precedence with the existing Session Accent toggle, theme changes and special input-mode colors. Preserve meaningful Bash/Python mode and warning/error colors rather than indiscriminately recoloring every state.
- Request a redraw when the override changes, and retain terminal color-capability handling.

## Current implementation

`packages/coding-agent/src/utils/session-color.ts` derives the accent from the session name and theme. `updateEditorBorderColor()` in `modes/interactive-mode.ts` uses it when `statusLine.sessionAccent` is enabled; disabling that setting falls back to reasoning-level theme colors.

Extensions can set a theme, but there is no dedicated session-accent override API. This request is for a narrow color-control contract, not a custom composer replacement or a new theme system.

### Description

`ctx.ui` exposes `setWorkingMessage`, `setWidget`, `setStatus`, etc., but there is no seam to customize the **working indicator / spinner** itself (glyph or animation) while a turn is streaming. Verified absent on 18.0.0 and 18.0.1 via extension probe.

Extensions that provide custom-themed UIs currently cannot style or animate the spinner glyph. Extensions / Plugins

1. Expose `ctx.ui.setWorkingIndicator(fn | string)` mirroring `setWorkingMessage`, or

### Alternatives Considered

Modifying the working message directly with embedded SGR sequences (`\x1b[...]`), but the terminal renderer strips or leaks control sequences in this context.

### Environment

- omp 18.0.1, Windows x64 (official release binary)
- Extension API via TS extension host

issues.title: TUI: composer shows raw markdown source while the sent message renders it as Markdown
issues.body:
## Description

The input field and the transcript render the same message text differently. While typing,
the composer paints the raw markdown source — backtick code spans appear literally
(`` `<-<-` ``, `` `Agent Hub` ``) in one flat text style. After submitting, the transcript
renders that same string as Markdown: backticks are consumed and the code-span contents are
painted in the `mdCode` color, with emphasis/HTML-entity/math transforms applied as well.
The message visibly "changes shape" on send, and the composer gives no indication of the
final rendering.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the interactive TUI.
2. In the composer, type a message containing inline code spans, e.g.
   `` `<-<-` -> opens `Agent Hub` -> press `Ctrl`+`S` ``.
3. Observe the input field: delimiters literal, uniform styling.
4. Submit with <kbd>Enter</kbd> (a `/skill:<name>` invocation shows the same text in the
   skill card body; a plain message shows it in the user bubble).
5. Compare the transcript row against the composer row.

## Expected Behavior

The input field and the sent message draw the same text the same way — either the composer
previews the Markdown the transcript will render, or the transcript shows what the composer
showed.

## Root Cause

Two independent renderers with no shared contract for user-authored text:

- **Composer paint path** — `packages/tui/src/components/editor.ts` (`render` ≈ :1212-1301,
  row styling :1461-1468) driven by `packages/tui/src/prompt/custom-editor.ts`
  (`decorateText`). It paints the buffer literally; no markdown interpretation exists
  anywhere on this path.
- **Transcript path** — `packages/tui/src/chat/user-message.ts:133-136` and
  `packages/tui/src/chat/skill-message.ts:148-153` wrap the same string in the `Markdown`
  component (`packages/tui/src/components/markdown.ts`), whose inline renderer consumes
  code-span delimiters and recolors the content (`markdown.ts:3206-3210` →
  `theme.fg("mdCode", …)` in `theme/tui-adapters.ts:207`).

```ts
// packages/tui/src/chat/user-message.ts:133 — sent message: Markdown-rendered
const md = new Markdown(text, 1, 1, getMarkdownTheme(), {
    bgColor,
    color: userBubbleColor(options, composerTokenRegex(mentionLabels)),
});

// packages/tui/src/components/editor.ts — composer: raw buffer, flat text style;
// no Markdown component on the paint path (decorateText only injects SGR decorations)
```

This also explains the glyph-level difference visible in terminals with coding-font
ligatures: both surfaces emit the same ASCII `<-`/`->`, but in the composer they sit next to
literal backticks in one flat span, while in the transcript they sit beside `mdCode`-colored
spans with the delimiters gone — so the ligature runs read differently before and after send.

## Environment

- **Platform:** Linux
- **omp version:** omp/18.3.0
- **Bun version:** 1.4.2
- **Area:** TUI / Display

## Additional context

Byte-level reproduction on a real PTY (tmux, default theme). Source string recovered
verbatim from the session JSONL — `` `<-<-` -> opens `Agent Hub` -> … ``:

- composer cell content + SGR: `ESC[38;2;229;229;231m` followed by `` `<-<-` -> opens `Agent Hub` -> … `` —
  single flat span, delimiters literal
- sent skill card body: `ESC[38;2;125;138;199m<-<-` `ESC[38;2;229;229;231m -> opens `
  `ESC[38;2;125;138;199mAgent Hub` … — delimiters consumed, code spans colored

Related but distinct: #7602 (skill args whitespace-collapsed in the card — same component,
different defect), #5559 (inverse ask on collab-web: plain text instead of markdown), #8582
(fixed wrap-time inline-code style bleed).

## Description

In OMP TUI (v15.8.0), when new content is loaded — such as after context compaction, message streaming, or session resume — the message list scrolls back to the top instead of staying at or scrolling to the latest message. This requires the user to manually scroll down after every content update.

## Expected behavior

The TUI should either:
1. Automatically scroll to the latest (bottom) message when new content is added, or
2. Stay at the current scroll position without resetting to the top

Add a TUI configuration option (e.g. `tui.autoScrollToBottom` or `tui.followMode`) that controls whether the viewport follows new content to the bottom. Default could be `true` (follow) to match the behavior users expect from chat-like interfaces.

- OMP version: omp/15.8.0
- Terminal: xterm-256color (TERM=xterm-256color)
- Config: `tui.hyperlinks = off`, `display.shimmer = disabled`
- No existing config option controls scroll behavior

issues.title: TUI: add an option to preserve detailed tool cards under viewport pressure
issues.body:
## Summary

Since the capacity-driven transcript viewport introduced in 18.0.1, active tool cards may collapse into one-line compact indicators when the live viewport is under pressure.

This behavior makes sense for preserving assistant text, especially after #9718 / #9723, but there is currently no user-facing option to prefer detailed tool visibility instead.

For workflows where the user actively supervises shell commands, reads, greps, edits, and subagent activity, collapsing tool cards to a single summary row removes useful execution context.

## Current behavior

Under viewport pressure, tool activity can collapse to compact rows such as:

```text
• Bash ...
• Read ...
• Glob ...
```

This is intentional presentation behavior in the current transcript allocator.

The existing `Ctrl+O` expansion state does not fully solve this because viewport allocation can still force an active tool block into its compact representation.

There also does not appear to be a configuration escape hatch for choosing a different pressure policy.

## Requested behavior

Add a setting that controls how tool activity is treated under viewport pressure.

For example:

```yaml
display:
  toolPressureMode: assistant-first
```

Possible values:

- `assistant-first`
  - Current behavior.
  - Preserve conversational text first.
  - Collapse tool cards aggressively when space is constrained.

- `balanced`
  - Allow tool cards to retain a small multi-line preview where possible.

- `tool-detail-first`
  - Prefer retaining the normal detailed tool card presentation.
  - Allow more conversational transcript text to leave the live viewport instead of collapsing active tool cards to one-line indicators.

The exact setting name and values are flexible. The main request is for a supported way to opt out of aggressive tool-card compaction.

## Motivation

Some users treat tool execution as an important part of the live interface rather than background activity.

For long-running coding tasks, being able to see:

- the command currently running;
- recent command output;
- file paths being read;
- grep/search context;
- edit previews;
- subagent activity;

is often more useful than keeping additional assistant prose visible in the constrained live viewport.

The current policy makes a reasonable default, but it optimizes for one supervision style.

## Compatibility

The default should remain the current assistant-first behavior so existing users and the fix from #9718 / #9723 are unaffected.

This would only add an explicit user-selectable presentation policy.

## Related

- #9718
- #9723
- #9483
issues.display_title: TUI: add an option to preserve detailed tool cards under viewport pressure

issues.title: feat(tui): make the 30 FPS render cap configurable up to 120 FPS
issues.body:
## Description

OMP currently caps ordinary TUI renders at 30 FPS:

```ts
static readonly #MIN_RENDER_INTERVAL_MS = 1000 / 30;
```

`#scheduleRender()` then adds adaptive backpressure from the previous frame cost and terminal output backlog. Forced repaint gestures can run immediately, but streaming, animations, and ordinary state changes share the 30 FPS cadence.

That is a sound default, especially after the idle-CPU work in #5192/#5193, but it also hard-caps visibly changing UI on 60–240 Hz terminals. Modern TUI renderers such as OpenTUI separate a steady `targetFps` from a higher `maxFps` and document configurations such as 60/120 FPS: https://opentui.com/docs/core-concepts/renderer/#choose-a-render-schedule

A TUI cannot discover or synchronize to the physical monitor's refresh rate through standard terminal protocols. DEC 2026 synchronized output, which OMP already supports, makes each terminal update atomic; it is not display vsync and does not report 540/1000 Hz. The actionable control is therefore an explicit render cap, not automatic monitor matching.

## Use Case

On a high-refresh display and fast local terminal emulator, cursor movement, streamed text, shimmer, and other changing rows should be able to update above 30 FPS when the user opts in. The default must remain battery- and CPU-friendly, and idle/event-driven screens must remain idle rather than running a continuous frame loop.

## Area

TUI / Display

## Proposed Solution

Make the ordinary render cadence configurable with a conservative bounded setting, for example:

```yaml
display:
  maxFps: 120 # default: 30; supported range: 15..120
```

Implementation constraints:

- Keep 30 FPS as the default.
- Keep rendering demand-driven; this setting only changes the minimum interval when a render is already pending.
- Preserve adaptive backpressure (`lastFrameCostMs * 2`), the 200 ms responsiveness cap, output-backlog coalescing, and DEC 2026 frame bracketing.
- Clamp the supported value to 120 FPS. A 540/1000 FPS ANSI producer would have a 1.85/1 ms total budget and would mostly create CPU/PTY pressure while the terminal emulator still controls presentation.
- Thread the configured cadence into `TUIOptions`/the render scheduler rather than reading settings inside the hot path.
- Add deterministic scheduler tests for the default 33.3 ms floor, an opted-in 8.3 ms floor, adaptive slow-frame backpressure, and unchanged idle behavior.
- Add a small render benchmark before considering a higher cap.

Would maintainers accept an explicit bounded `maxFps`, or should high-refresh support remain a library-level `TUIOptions` capability for embedders before it becomes a user setting?

## Alternatives Considered

- **Match the monitor refresh rate automatically:** terminal applications do not receive a standard display refresh-rate signal, and synchronized-output mode is not vsync.
- **Set 120 FPS globally:** regresses laptop/SSH/tmux CPU behavior and ignores the rationale behind #5192.
- **Allow 540/1000 FPS:** unrealistic for the full synchronous compose/diff/write path and unlikely to produce distinct displayed frames.
- **Leave the 30 FPS constant:** simplest and safest, but prevents experimentation on fast local terminals even though OMP already has demand-driven rendering, partial/direct-write paths, output coalescing, and adaptive load shedding.
issues.display_title: feat(tui): make the 30 FPS render cap configurable up to 120 FPS

issues.title: Setting to cap collapsed tool-output preview lines (collapsed state scales with terminal height, no floor knob)
issues.body:
## Problem

`Ctrl+O` (`app.tools.expand`) toggles tool-output blocks between expanded and collapsed. But the **collapsed** state is not a fixed, compact budget — the generic tool-result renderer (`Gv` / `eq()` in `packages/coding-agent`) computes the collapsed line budget as:

```
max(6, terminal_rows - 20)
```

So on a taller terminal, the *collapsed* preview grows proportionally:

| Terminal rows | Collapsed budget |
|---|---|
| 24 | 6 lines |
| 40 | 20 lines |
| 50 | 30 lines |
| 80 | 60 lines |

A `read` of an internal resource (e.g. `omp://hooks.md`, ~345 lines) on a 50-row terminal shows ~30 lines of content + a `… 337 more lines [Ctrl+O: Expand]` hint. The collapsed state is nearly as tall as the viewport — defeating the point of collapsing.

This is separate from (and larger than) the fixed `OUTPUT_COLLAPSED = 3` constant, which only governs a few specific renderers (`bash` log tail, the memory tool). Most tool results go through `Gv`/`eq()`.

## What I'd like

A setting to cap the collapsed preview line budget — ideally one where `0` means "tool name only, zero output lines." Something like:

```yaml
tools.collapsedPreviewLines: 0   # 0 = name only; -1 = today's terminal-height scaling; N = cap
```

- `0` → collapsed shows just the tool name + a `… N more lines [Ctrl+O: Expand]` hint, no content lines
- `N` → collapsed shows at most N tail lines
- unset / `-1` → current behavior (`max(6, rows - 20)`)

## Why

The terminal-height scaling makes sense as a *default* (use available space), but on large monitors the collapsed state is too tall to be a useful "summary" view. Users who want a compact transcript — see just which tools ran, not their output — have no way to get there: `read.toolResultPreview` only affects inline file-content rendering for `read`, not the generic collapsed budget; `tools.artifactSpillThreshold` offloads to artifacts but doesn't shrink the inline tail; `Ctrl+O` itself is the toggle, not a cap.

Related: #2416 (auto-collapse on turn completion) — both asks are about making the collapsed state more useful. A configurable cap is the smaller, more general primitive.

## Environment

omp: latest (v15.9.x line), verified by reading the bundled `cli.js` — `eq()` is `max(Gh6=6, rows - jh6=20)`, call sites in the generic `Gv` preview limiter used by most tool-result renderers.
issues.display_title: Setting to cap collapsed tool-output preview lines (collapsed state scales with terminal height, no floor knob)

issues.title: Permanent event-loop wedge at 100% CPU after escalating ui.loop-blocked during 9-subagent runs; all subagents starve, process never recovers
issues.body:
### Description

During a `task` batch running **9 in-process subagents**, the main process enters escalating synchronous event-loop blocks (`ui.loop-blocked`, tagged `subagent:<id>`) whose duration roughly doubles each time — 0.5s → 1s → 2.3s → 12s → 48.5s → 82.4s — until one block **never returns**. The process then sits at 100% CPU on the main thread indefinitely (observed 3+ hours / 189 CPU-minutes on one occurrence), with:

- zero outbound provider connections (`lsof`: only a localhost MCP socket + the python tool bridge) while nominally running 9 subagents,
- zero log writes, zero session-file writes,
- all 9 subagent transcripts stalled mid-turn (each ends on a `toolResult`, i.e. waiting to send its next model request),
- TUI completely frozen; the loop watchdog itself starved (the final block is never logged because the log line is emitted only when a block *ends*).

macOS `sample` during the wedge: all 2,204 samples on the main thread inside one synchronous JS call stack (anonymous JIT frames; bun binary is symbol-stripped). Worker threads idle. So this is a runaway synchronous JS section, not I/O or lock contention.

**It happened twice in one day, in the same workflow, on the same machine** — same signature, different subagent batch (a "Review" round at 17:22, an "R2" round at 20:15). Both wedged while the phase breadcrumb pointed at the same (largest-transcript) subagent of the batch.

**Correlated trigger:** right before the terminal wedge, several subagents' turns failed with `OpenAI completions stream timed out while waiting for the first event` (custom OpenAI-completions provider via a local proxy; upstream intermittently stalls before the first SSE byte — verified independently with curl). Each failure produced an empty `stopReason: "error"` assistant turn → `agent_end` maintenance routing → auto-retry. The wedge follows this error/retry storm.

Note the feedback loop: once loop blocks exceed the first-event timeout (48s and 82s blocks observed vs. a first-event window), omp can *manufacture* further stream timeouts itself — while the loop is blocked, SSE reads and timers starve, so in-flight streams "time out", producing more error turns, more retries, more subagent events to process synchronously, longer blocks. 17:22:04  ui.loop-blocked 22765ms  phase=subagent:ExecTruthReview  <- last line; wedged for 3+ hours until SIGTERM

Workload shape: parent session jsonl ~8.2MB after ~2h; 9 subagent transcripts 0.44–1.08MB each (44–155 lines — large `grep`/`read`/`eval` tool results over ~1MB data files). Subagent models mixed, several on a custom OpenAI-completions provider at xhigh reasoning.

### Steps to Reproduce

No minimal repro yet — happened twice out of two runs of this workflow, so the shape reproduces reliably here:

1. `task` batch with 9 in-process subagents, several on an OpenAI-completions provider whose upstream intermittently stalls before the first SSE event (a local proxy to ChatGPT-backend models in our case; anything that triggers `stream timed out while waiting for the first event` should do).
2. Subagents do heavy tool work producing large tool results (grep/read over ~1MB files), growing each transcript to ~1MB.
3. Let it run 1–2 hours (parent session several MB).
4. Watch `ui.loop-blocked` warnings tagged `subagent:*` escalate (roughly doubling), then stop appearing entirely while CPU pins at 100% — permanent wedge.

### Expected Behavior

- Per-subagent-event synchronous work in the parent should be bounded (not scale with accumulated transcript/session size), so blocks stay in the ms range.
- A block that exceeds some sanity ceiling should be breakable/detectable — currently the watchdog can only report a block after it ends, so a terminal block is invisible and the process burns a core forever with no logging.
- Stream first-event timeouts should account for self-inflicted loop starvation (a 48–82s blocked loop must not translate into "provider timed out" → error turn → retry storm).

### Error Output

```shell
# escalating blocks (both occurrences) — see timeline above

# subagent turn failures immediately before terminal wedge:
"OpenAI completions stream timed out while waiting for the first event" (model gpt-5.6-sol, api openai-completions)

# maintenance routing for those turns:
agent_end maintenance routing route=entered stopReason=error provider=vibeproxy model=gpt-5.6-sol contentBlocks=0 hasToolCalls=false hasText=false

# process state during wedge:
# - ps: R state, 100.0% CPU, main thread only
# - /usr/bin/sample: 2204/2204 samples in one synchronous JS stack (JIT frames, symbol-stripped)
# - lsof: no provider sockets; only localhost MCP client socket + python tool bridge listener
# - no writes to omp log or any session jsonl after the last line above
```

### Platform

macOS

### omp version

16.4.8

### Bun version

1.3.14

### Provider

Custom (models.yml)

### Area

Other

### Additional context

- The 16.2.2 changelog entry — "Fixed TUI thought stream stalling and `ui.loop-blocked` warnings during subagent-heavy runs by optimizing the mid-run compaction persistence check" — and the comments in `agent-session.ts` around `#indexPersistedMessageKeys` / `#persistTurnMessagesForMidRunCompaction` (“the load-bearing source of the `ui.loop-blocked` warnings in the bug report”) fixed one superlinear path in this same bug class. 16.4.8 includes that fix, so this is a second, distinct superlinear/non-terminating path. The doubling block durations suggest per-event work proportional to accumulated data.
- Phase attribution caveat: `takeRecentLoopPhase` reports the most recent breadcrumb, so the blocking code isn't necessarily inside `processEvent` in `task/executor.ts` — only in the same starved stretch as subagent event handling (e.g. progress render, session persistence, retry handling are all candidates).
- Possibly related to the render-side costs profiled in #5230 (`wrapTextWithAnsi`/`stringWidth` dominating CPU during subagent-heavy runs), but this report is about unbounded/terminal blocks, not steady-state overhead.
- Both wedged processes' full session directories (parent jsonl + 9 subagent jsonl each) are preserved and available on request, as are the complete logs.

issues.title: Add concise tool display mode for low-noise steering
issues.body:
## Problem

Oh My Pi's TUI currently exposes detailed tool invocations by default. That is useful for debugging, but it creates visual noise when a user is steering an agent through a longer task and only needs to know what tool is running, whether it is active or complete, and the minimal context needed to follow progress.

## Use case

As a user supervising a busy session, I want a low-noise tool display mode so I can scan intent and status quickly while still expanding a specific tool call when I need the full command, code, query, or output details.

## Area

TUI / Display; Configuration; Tools

## Proposed behavior

Add a configuration setting:

```toml
tools.displayMode = "detailed"
```

Supported values:

- `detailed`: current behavior; show full tool call details inline by default.
- `concise`: collapsed tool cards hide command/code/query/output details by default while keeping intent, status, tool identity, and minimal metadata visible.

Default should remain `detailed` to preserve existing behavior.

In `concise` mode, full details should remain available by expanding the tool call with Ctrl+O, matching the existing expansion affordance rather than removing information.

## Alternatives considered

- Global truncation of tool output: reduces noise but also loses context and does not hide sensitive/noisy command or query details consistently.
- Per-tool hardcoded compact rendering: handles some noisy tools but creates inconsistent UI behavior and more maintenance paths.
- Changing the default display globally: lower noise for some users but would be a breaking behavior change for users relying on detailed inline tool visibility.
issues.display_title: Add concise tool display mode for low-noise steering
